== Generating retro arcade game-style music with Magenta.js

https://dev.to/t/audio[[.crayons-tag__prefix]##++#++##audio]
https://dev.to/t/gamedev[[.crayons-tag__prefix]##++#++##gamedev]
https://dev.to/t/javascript[[.crayons-tag__prefix]##++#++##javascript]

[[article-body]]
In this article, games from the early 1980s or so are considered retro
arcade games. Examples are Xevious and DigDug. The BGM of retro arcade
games of these days often consisted of repeating short phrases of about
4 to 8 bars.

I thought I would like to have such BGM for my mini-games and, if
possible, generate it automatically. Therefore, I was looking for a
technology to create such BGM.

https://tones.wolfram.com/about/how-it-works[WolframTones] is one such
technology. WolframTones cuts out cellular automaton and turns them into
melodies. It can easily create a variety of songs. However, it doesn't
seem easy to reproduce specific phrases often seen in old games, such as
a bass that reciprocates in perfect fifths with sixteenth notes, due to
the characteristics of a cellular automaton.

An example of the latest technology is OpenAI's
https://openai.com/blog/jukebox/[Jukebox]. However, this is not intended
for retro games, as it generates musical waveforms, not musical scores.

The following technology I looked into was
https://magenta.tensorflow.org/[Magenta], a research project by Google
that applies machine learning to music and pictures.
https://hello-magenta.glitch.me/[Magenta.js] is available as an
implementation that can run in the Magenta browser.

Magenta.js has
https://magenta.github.io/magenta-js/music/classes/_music_rnn_model_.musicrnn.html[MusicRNN],
which automatically generates the following phrases when entering a
musical score. I thought that if I gave it a short score of a retro
game, it would create another song like the background music of the
retro game. So, I tried to prototype the following.

* https://abagames.itch.io/short-vgm-generator[Short VGM generator]

Pressing the "Generate" button in the center of the screen generates a
new phrase based on the phrase on the left of the screen. The generated
phrase is displayed on the right side of the screen and played back.
Although it is a simple phrase generation consisting of only two tracks
(melody and bass), it can create music like retro game background music.

One problem is that I could not figure out how to input multiple tracks
as original phrases in Magenta.js. Therefore, I created separate phrases
for the melody and bass. I also adjusted the sound of the bass when the
bass was dissonant with the melody. The bass sound is adjusted so that
the frequency of the melody sound is in the ratio of 1 to 4. Unchecking
the checkbox at the bottom of the screen eliminates this adjustment,
thus generating a freer phrase.

Another problem was that the Magenta.js built-in player was not capable
of simultaneous speech. Therefore, I use
https://tonejs.github.io/[Tone.js] for playback. I also find it easier
to input phrases using MML, so I use
https://github.com/mohayonao/mml-iterator[mml-iterator] to parse MML and
convert it into a form that Magenta.js can handle.

Please refer to the following repository if you wish to use the
generated BGM in your game.

=== image:./index_files/github-logo-5a155e1f9a670af7944dd5e12375bc76ed542ea80224905ecaf878b9157cdefc.svg[GitHub logo] https://github.com/abagames[abagames] / https://github.com/abagames/good-old-game-sound-generator[good-old-game-sound-generator]

==== Generate sound effects and background music for good old-fashioned mini-games

[[readme]]
== https://github.com/abagames/good-old-game-sound-generator#good-old-game-sound-generator-demo[good-old-game-sound-generator (]https://abagames.github.io/good-old-game-sound-generator/build/[DEMO])

Generate sound effects and background music for good old-fashioned
mini-games. Powered by https://magenta.tensorflow.org/[magenta.js] and
https://github.com/loov/jsfx[jsfx].

[[user-content-how-to-generate-background-music]]
=== https://github.com/abagames/good-old-game-sound-generator#how-to-generate-background-music[How to generate background music]

. Open the
https://abagames.github.io/good-old-game-sound-generator/build/[DEMO]
page.
. (Optional) Input the base music for the generation in
https://github.com/mohayonao/mml-iterator[MML (Music Macro Language)] at
the bottom of the screen.
. Click the 'Generate' button.

[[user-content-how-to-use-the-generated-music-in-your-game]]
=== https://github.com/abagames/good-old-game-sound-generator#how-to-use-the-generated-music-in-your-game[How to use the generated music in your game]

. Import
https://github.com/abagames/sounds-some-sounds[sounds-some-sounds] or
https://github.com/abagames/crisp-game-lib[crisp-game-lib] library.
. On the Demo page, click the 'Copy to clipboard' button to copy the MML
strings to your clipboard.
. Call the `sss.playMml` function with the MML strings in the clipboard
as the first argument.

It would be nice to generate sound effects similarly, but since MusicRNN
is only intended to create melodies, it does not seem possible to take
the same approach.

* http://www.losdoggies.com/archives/1302[Super Mario Melodies]

The above article has a score of Super Mario Bros. sound effects. The
game's sound effects are too specific to be seen in a musical score.
Therefore, finding relevant research on sound effect generation methods
based on musical scores is probably tricky. Most of the existing sound
effect generation tools are based on
http://www.drpetter.se/project_sfxr.html[sfxr]-based waveform generation
methods, and I have not seen any that generate them as musical scores.
Further research is needed on automatic sound effect generation for
retro games.
